Resources, succession, family groups, age of majority and court offices follow the game’s rules. They do not describe attested historical values. Claims to the throne could pass through both paternal and maternal kin and lead to competing dynastic claims; both of the game’s succession laws simplify this. The source material attests no household at the court. The three courtiers are generated for the game.

Resources, succession, family groups, age of majority and court offices follow the game’s rules. They do not describe attested historical values. The Capetians give the king’s son precedence through dynastic succession; the game’s primogeniture simplifies designation, coronation and the historical male line. Philip’s wedding to Agnes in 1196 and his continuing marriage dispute with Ingeborg require more legal relationship statuses than a single spouse record. The code indicates this limitation, not a canonically approved system of polygamy. The game allows one spouse per person. The court shows at most one marriage for each person.

Resources, succession, family groups, age of majority and court offices follow the game’s rules. They do not describe attested historical values. The dynasty appoints heirs and has also replaced a designated son and elected a caliph; neither the game’s automatic primogeniture nor the council’s purely merit-based selection represents this. The game’s election order chooses first among adults in the ruler’s house by ability, then among the house’s children by age and last among the court’s other adults by ability. A child rules through a regent. If no one is eligible, a generated person from outside the court is chosen. The election does not represent the council’s or the electors’ own arrangements. The source material attests no household at the court. The three courtiers are generated for the game.

Einhard lists Charles’s conquests for the whole reign without years, and the Royal Frankish Annals show his itinerary in 800. Barcelona lies outside the shape: Zatun entrusted the city to Charles in 797, but on the bookmark date it was under a two-year siege that ended in the summer of 801, outside Frankish hands. Venice lies within the shape: its dukes came to Charles in 806, Pippin attacked the city in 810, and Charles gave it to Nikephoros in the peace that same year. Brittany’s submission in 799 did not last. Uniform rule is not attested. Pippin and Louis were anointed kings in Italy and Aquitaine in 781; the map does not distinguish their territories from Charles’s.
